title: Repair the three production defects found by Investigation 035 (S1 dead simulator URL, S3 shadowed polygon-offset engine, S4 legacy DXF 500s)
intent: Investigation 035 (evidence packet, Consolidation Lab PR #19) found three live defects by driving production entrypoints. This PR repairs them and adds guards that can actually fail on each one. S1: five frontend call sites posted to /api/cam/simulate_gcode, which is not mounted; they are repointed to the two endpoints that match their two different contracts. S3: the N17 utility handler shadowed the governed polygon-offset engine at POST /api/cam/polygon_offset.nc, applying stepover as millimetres instead of a fraction of tool_dia; the utility route is renamed so the governed draft lane owns its URL. S4: try_build_with_ezdxf raised instead of returning None, severing the ASCII R12 fallback its callers depend on and 500ing both legacy DXF export endpoints.

diff_articulation.what_changed: S1 (frontend only): four JSON call sites move from /api/cam/simulate_gcode to /api/cam/sim/gcode; one multipart call site moves to /api/cam/sim/upload. No backend route is added or removed for S1. S3: app/cam/routers/utility/polygon_router.py changes its route path from /polygon_offset.nc to /polygon_offset_n17.nc; the handler, its request model and its millimetre stepover semantics are untouched, so nothing is deleted. S4: dxf_helpers.try_build_with_ezdxf calls custom_vars.append('COMMENT', comment) with two positional args instead of a tuple, emits polylines through dxf_compat.add_polyline(version='R12') instead of msp.add_lwpolyline (invalid in R12), and its outer guard catches TypeError and ezdxf.DXFError so the function returns None on failure as its callers require. Plus two regression suites.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: All three are behaviour changes on live endpoints, and none is covered by an existing gate. The existing test_polygon_offset_endpoint_smoke.py asserted only status 200 and that the body contains 'G' for /api/cam/polygon_offset.nc; it passed throughout the period the wrong engine served that URL because its assertions cannot distinguish two G-code generators. The new backend suite pins the property that was wrong (pass inset equals tool_dia * stepover, the X-ToolBox-Lane owner header, and preview/NC agreement) and 7 of its 11 tests fail against the pre-fix tree. S1 is invisible to pytest because no backend route was ever wrong, so its guard is a vitest that scans client sources; 3 of its 4 assertions fail against the pre-fix frontend. S4 additionally pins the return-None fallback contract that WP-1 exception narrowing (c3147212) severed.
diff_articulation.behavior_change_detail: POST /api/cam/polygon_offset.nc now returns the governed draft-lane toolpath (X-ToolBox-Lane: draft) instead of N17 output. For the documented consumer contract this is a correction, not a regression: with tool_dia 6.0 and stepover 0.4 the pass inset changes from 0.4 mm to 2.4 mm, which is what both live consumers already implied and what /polygon_offset.preview already returned. Callers who genuinely want the millimetre-stepover N17 engine use POST /api/cam/polygon_offset_n17.nc. Both legacy DXF export endpoints change from HTTP 500 to HTTP 200 returning readable R12 DXF.

files.intent: Client guard for S1. The defect is invisible to the backend suite because no backend route was ever wrong, so this scans client sources for the dead URL and pins each caller to the endpoint matching its contract.
This PR's own CBSP21 declaration. No CBSP21 policy, schema, threshold or checker change.

findings.note: POST /api/cam/polygon_offset.nc changes which handler serves it. Mitigation: both live consumers (OffsetLabView.vue, api/n17_n18.ts) already declare the governed fraction convention and already preview against the governed-only /polygon_offset.preview, so neither loses a contract it was relying on. The N17 implementation is renamed, not deleted, and is covered by its own regression test.

Legacy DXF exports go from 500 to 200. Output is the ASCII R12 writer, which is what these endpoints produced before WP-1 exception narrowing (c3147212) broke the fallback. try_build_with_ezdxf still returns None at runtime due to a separate BytesIO/StringIO fault documented in the PR; that path is left dormant rather than activated, because switching the writer for legacy exports would need CAD-viewer verification per the project DXF standard.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Both medium findings are inherent to repairing the defects and are covered by tests that fail against the pre-fix tree. RMOS, Manufacturing Spine, CBSP21 checkers, the Vectorizer and dump_and_assert_routes.py are unchanged.
architecture_scan.notes: Investigation 035 evidence lives in Consolidation Lab PR #19. This PR is the production remediation it unblocked; the two are deliberately in different repositories because Investigation 033 makes Luthier's Toolbox the read-only subject of legacy-wiring evidence.
